researchQuestion: In this fixed exploratory matrix, does the released Carrylog product bundle (canonical context, generated router surfaces, and a runner-verified resume envelope) show a beneficial continuation direction over repository-only discovery without item-level regressions against the same prior-session packet delivered as a concise manual handoff?

hypotheses.signal: Within each harness, Carrylog resume has a beneficial direction over repository-only discovery on relevant-fact recall, contradictions, prohibited reversals, repeated work, unnecessary clarification, and task completion.
hypotheses.manualBaseline: Within each harness, every preregistered item-level Carrylog regression against manual handoff is retained and reported; Tier 1 is regression screening, not a formal non-inferiority test.
hypotheses.stop: Apply the frozen Tier 2 STOP, GO, then REDESIGN precedence without narrative override; retain repository-memory governance as the supported value unless the GO criteria pass.

claude.modelFamily: GPT through an Anthropic-compatible JM Router route

controls.promptLanguage: Match each repository's canonical documentation language: English for Carrylog and Korean for BusyCafe.
controls.networkBoundary: Provider API control-plane traffic is required for the harness. Model tools and registered verification subprocesses may not access network endpoints; the macOS runner and verification wrapper enforce and canary-test this boundary.
controls.evaluatorMasking: Randomized blind IDs and behavior-only bundles hide run order and harness metadata, but condition may remain inferable from substantive output; this exploratory pilot records that limitation.
controls.deliveryPacketControl: Manual and Carrylog conditions use the same separately frozen six-section packet. Carrylog additionally exposes the released product bundle: canonical project/current-state context, generated router and Skill surfaces, and the deterministic resume/Git envelope. This pilot estimates that full bundle, not an isolated envelope-format effect or automatic checkpoint authorship.
controls.conditionOrderPolicy: Fixture-harness blocks are SHA-256 ordered. Each harness-repository stratum uses five of the six condition permutations exactly once; the omitted permutations for its two repositories are derangements. Therefore every condition's position counts differ by at most one globally, within each harness, and within each harness-repository stratum.

tier2DecisionRule.contrastDefinition: Exactly 40 contrast vectors: 2 harnesses x 10 fixtures x 2 comparators (repository-only and manual-handoff). One vector is screenable only when Carrylog and its comparator both have finite outcomes for all six primary metrics.
tier2DecisionRule.favorableOrientation: Recall and task completion are favorable when Carrylog minus comparator is positive; contradictions, prohibited reversals, repeated work, and unnecessary clarification are multiplied by -1 before comparison so positive is always favorable.
tier2DecisionRule.stop: STOP if any reviewed Carrylog-resume run has a scored sensitive exposure or any privacy rejection; or if both harnesses have an adverse macro paired mean against repository-only on the same three or more of the six primary metrics; or if the same manual-regression item for the same fixture is flagged in both harnesses. A Carrylog privacy rejection is conservatively safety-significant regardless of its reviewer reason code. Missing or protocol-invalid evidence alone does not trigger STOP.
tier2DecisionRule.go: GO to Tier 2 only if all 60 runs have reviewed terminal artifacts with zero protocol-invalid runs, all 40 preregistered contrast vectors are screenable, every Carrylog-resume sensitive-exposure and prohibited-reversal outcome is available and zero, the manual-handoff regression screen has zero missing pairs, unavailable items, or flags, and in each harness all six macro paired means against repository-only are non-adverse with at least two strictly favorable means.
tier2DecisionRule.redesign: REDESIGN is mandatory for every result that satisfies neither STOP nor GO. REDESIGN includes missing pairs, provider attrition, isolated or non-replicated regression flags, inconsistent harness direction, and a valid but insufficiently favorable signal.
tier2DecisionRule.noPostOutcomeOverride: Apply STOP first, then GO, then REDESIGN. Explanations may contextualize inputs but may not delete flags, change thresholds, or override the resulting class. Any amended rule requires a new frozen protocol and new runs.

analysisRules.primaryAggregation: Macro-average normalized task outcomes within harness; never pool raw fact weights across tasks.
analysisRules.descriptiveInterval: Fixed-seed fixture bootstrap 95% interval with 10000 resamples; it describes selected-fixture variation only.
analysisRules.manualRegressionRule: Flag every item where manual receives a continuity-eligible fact or completion criterion and Carrylog does not, or where Carrylog adds a contradiction, prohibited reversal, repeated-work event, unnecessary clarification, or sensitive exposure. Explanations never delete flags.
analysisRules.missingness: Never coerce unavailable evidence to zero or weight by evaluator confidence. Report attrition and availability denominators by condition.

reviewGate.reviewableDigest: SHA-256 over the exact sorted frozen input path, byte length, and file digest tuples, excluding freeze-manifest.json, review-attestations.json, and observed-result surfaces. Excluding the attestation file prevents self-reference.
reviewGate.attestationContract: First set status=frozen. Then replace the pending null digest and empty reviews with the printed reviewDigest and exactly two review objects. Each object has only reviewerId, an explicit independenceStatement, verdict=GO, UTC reviewedAt, the same reviewDigest, and findings=[]. Reviewer IDs must be distinct.
reviewGate.machineGate: freeze --review-digest requires status=frozen, no observed results, and passed Codex and Claude authenticated-canary attestations bound to the current harness-critical bytes. It then runs structural validation plus deterministic order and evaluation-bundle checks before printing the self-reference-free review input. freeze --write repeats those checks, recomputes the digest, and requires two distinct GO attestations over that exact digest before creating the manifest.

freezeRule: The unique first Git ADD commit of freeze-manifest.json is the permanent preregistration boundary. The manifest, its frozen inputs, and review attestations may not be deleted, re-added, or changed after that commit; amendments require a new experiment.
